title: Prime-to-Sylow degree of the constants fixed field
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], $K/e$ a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and $\ell$ a prime different from $\operatorname{char}(e)$. Let a finite group $G$ act on $K$ by $e$-automorphisms, where finite means finite underlying set [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set]. Assume that $E=K^G=\{x\in K:gx=x\text{ for all }g\in G\}$ is purely inseparable over $e$. Let $L\leq G$ have $\ell$-power order and index prime to $\ell$, and set $F=K^L$. Then $F/e$ is finite of degree prime to $\ell$, and $K/F$ is finite Galois with automorphism group exactly the image of $L$ in $\operatorname{Aut}_e(K)$, viewed as a group of $F$-automorphisms of $K$. Neither group action is assumed faithful. Degrees and finite, purely inseparable, and Galois field-extension terminology have their usual meanings: degree is vector-space dimension; purely inseparable means every element has some characteristic-power in the base, and equality with the base in characteristic zero; Galois means normal and separable [def-pc-field-tower].

proof.text: Let $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Aut}_e(K)$ be the action, $H=\rho(G)$ and $J=\rho(L)\leq H$. These are finite groups acting faithfully on $K$ by inclusion. The fixed-element equations give $K^H=E$ and $K^J=F$ and inclusions $e\subseteq E\subseteq F\subseteq K$. These are fields because sums, products and inverses of fixed elements remain fixed. Moreover $E/e$ and $F/e$ are finite: an $e$-linearly independent family in either subspace is linearly independent in $K$, hence has size at most $[K:e]$; successively adjoining vectors outside the span therefore terminates at a finite basis. An $e$-spanning family for $F$ is also an $E$-spanning family, so $F/E$ is finite.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 2, diagram (2.c), replacing possibly ineffective actions by their image; the fixed-field and finite-dimensional-subspace verifications are elementary.

proof.text: Apply [lem-wf-finite-field-action-fixed-degree] to the faithful actions of $H$ and $J$: $K/E$ and $K/F$ are finite Galois, with $[K:E]=|H|$ and $[K:F]=|J|$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field], the full group $A=\operatorname{Aut}_F(K)$ has order $[K:F]=|J|$. Each element of $J$ fixes $F$, giving an injection $J\hookrightarrow A$ which sends an automorphism to the identical underlying function. An injection between finite sets of the same size is surjective. Thus every $F$-automorphism of $K$ is the actual image of an element of $L$, and conversely every such image fixes $F$. This proves precisely the automorphism-group clause, without assuming either original action faithful.

source.place: Tag 09I3 (lemma-galois-over-fixed-field), applied to the two effective image groups; Tag 09I1 (lemma-finite-Galois), order of the full Galois group.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] to $E\subseteq F\subseteq K$. Substituting the preceding degrees gives $|H|=|J|[F:E]$. Apply [lem-sfb-surjective-subgroup-image-index] to the surjection $G\to H$ and subgroup $L$, to obtain $|H|=|J|[H:J]$ and $[H:J]\mid[G:L]$. Since $|J|>0$, cancellation gives $[F:E]=[H:J]$. Consequently $\ell\nmid[F:E]$: otherwise $\ell$ would divide $[G:L]$, contrary to the hypothesis.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.151, prime-to-ell degree of S1/L over S1/G1; Stacks Tag 09G9 (lemma-multiplicativity-degrees) for the field tower.

proof.text: If $\operatorname{char}(e)=0$, the purely inseparable hypothesis means $E=e$, hence $[E:e]=1$. If $\operatorname{char}(e)=p>0$, then $p$ is prime. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-pth-root-tower] to the finite purely inseparable extension $E/e$. Write its tower as $e=E_0\subseteq E_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq E_n=E$, where every $[E_i:E_{i-1}]=p$. Starting with $[E_0:e]=1$, repeated application of [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] yields $[E_i:e]=p^i$ for $i=0,\ldots,n$, including $n=0$. Since the distinct primes $p$ and $\ell$ do not divide one another, $\ell$ does not divide $p^n$. Thus in either characteristic $\ell\nmid[E:e]$.

source.place: Tag 09HI (lemma-finite-purely-inseparable), its degree-p tower; Tag 09G9 (lemma-multiplicativity-degrees); the characteristic-zero branch is the stated definition.

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] to $e\subseteq E\subseteq F$: $[F:e]=[F:E][E:e]$. Both factors are prime to $\ell$ by steps 3 and 4. If the prime $\ell$ divided their product it would divide one factor, so $[F:e]$ is prime to $\ell$. The finiteness of $F/e$ was established in step 1, and the finite Galois and exact image-group clauses were established in step 2.
